Millennial shopping is producing a split between where buying decisions begin and where purchases ultimately happen. The PYMNTS Intelligence report “The Millennial Shopping Map: How AI, Search and Stores Compete Before Checkout” found in July that Google remains the most widely used product-discovery tool among millennials, at 57%. However, ChatGPT has moved into second place […]
The post 41% of Millennials Use ChatGPT for Product Discovery appeared first on PYMNTS.com.
content: A recent PYMNTS Intelligence report reveals that 41 percent of millennials now use ChatGPT for product discovery, making it the second most popular tool for this purpose. While Google still leads at 57 percent, the trend highlights a growing shift in how younger consumers begin their shopping journeys through artificial intelligence rather than traditional search engines.

title: Merchants Put AI to Work Without Handing Over the Customer
summary:
The payments and retail industries are asking the wrong question about agentic commerce. The question is not whether an artificial intelligence agent can complete a purchase on its own, because many agents already can. It is whether the merchant wants to let one do so in the first place. The post Merchants Put AI to Work Without Handing Over the Customer appeared first on PYMNTS.com.
content: The payments and retail sectors are debating agentic commerce and whether artificial intelligence agents should be allowed to complete purchases independently. While many AI agents are already capable of making transactions, merchants face critical questions about whether they want to relinquish control over the customer relationship to automated systems, according to industry reports from PYMNTS.com.

title: Coldcard Wave 3 Operator Begins Cashing Out Stolen Bitcoin via THORChain and CoinJoin
summary: The operator behind the so-called Wave 3 cluster of Coldcard hardware-wallet thefts has begun systematically cashing out stolen bitcoin after weeks of inactivity, according to a Monday update from Galaxy Research. Galaxy’s on-chain team says the actor created 293 separate 2-of-2 multisignature vaults, one for... Read More
content: The operator of the Wave 3 Coldcard hardware wallet thefts has reportedly started cashing out stolen bitcoin after a period of inactivity. According to Galaxy Research, the actor has begun moving the funds using privacy-enhancing tools including THORChain and CoinJoin. Investigators continue to monitor the on-chain activity as the funds are systematically processed through these decentralized services.
